fix(aspire): resolve referenced modules only through the source mapping

GetReferencedModuleProjectPath probed seven current, ancestor, sibling and
root-level locations and silently returned a path that did not exist. It now
mirrors the workspace source mapping: when <root>/<Module>.slnx exists the
dependency is the consuming repository and resolves under <root>; otherwise it
resolves under the direct submodule <root>/references/<Module>. Any other case
throws InvalidOperationException naming the dependency and the expected path.

The rule runs through an internal overload with an injectable root, so tests
now cover the self, self-over-references, missing-self, mapped and five
unmapped layouts. Closes ledger entries DW-205 and DW-206.

Refs: Hexalith.Platform story 1.10

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@ -116,6 +116,57 @@ dotnet test tests/Hexalith.EventStore.Testing.Tests
 
 The solution file is `Hexalith.EventStore.slnx`.
 
+### Run and Debug in the Platform Workspace
+
+Run and debug EventStore as a module from the
+[Hexalith.Platform](https://github.com/Hexalith/Hexalith.Platform) workspace, where this repository is the
+direct submodule `references/Hexalith.EventStore`. Prerequisites:
+
+- The Platform-pinned `hexalith-module` tool, restored with `dotnet tool restore` in the Platform root.
+- Aspire CLI `13.6.1` exactly; the tool refuses any other version with `HXR015`.
+- A running Docker engine.
+- `HEXALITH_DAPR_HOME` set to an absolute, isolated Dapr home: Dapr CLI `1.18.0` at `tools/dapr` and runtime
+  `1.18.2` at `.dapr/bin/{daprd,placement,scheduler}`. The Platform README shows how to prepare one from the
+  official release assets.
+- The checkout's `HEAD` equal to the gitlink staged in the Platform repository. After a local commit here, run
+  `git add references/Hexalith.EventStore` in the Platform root before starting a run.
+
+From the Platform root:
+
+```bash
+export HEXALITH_DAPR_HOME="$HOME/.hexalith/dapr/1.18.2"
+dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- debug --manifest references/Hexalith.EventStore/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json
+```
+
+Pass the owner manifest under `references/`, never the Platform's copy in
+`src/Hexalith.Platform.Composition/Declarations/`. `debug` builds this checkout in Debug, starts only the
+`eventstore` gateway with its Dapr sidecar, the Dapr control plane and Redis, waits for the declared `/ready`
+endpoint, and reports the process id of the `dotnet run` launcher. The gateway is the launcher's child process:
+
+```bash
+ps --ppid <launcher-pid> -o pid,args
+```
+
+Attach to the child running `src/Hexalith.EventStore/bin/Debug/net10.0/Hexalith.EventStore`, for example with
+VS Code ("Attach to a .NET process"). Breakpoints in this checkout's sources bind. When you finish, stop only
+that run with:
+
+```bash
+dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- down --manifest references/Hexalith.EventStore/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json
+```
+
+`debug` does not print the run id: it is the file name of the run state `<runId>.json` under
+`${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/hexalith-builds/g4-runs/` on Linux. When an earlier run used the same manifest,
+`down --manifest` refuses with `HXR024`; pass the newest run's id with `--run-id`:
+
+```bash
+ls -t "${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}"/hexalith-builds/g4-runs/*.json | head -1
+dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- down --manifest references/Hexalith.EventStore/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json --run-id <runId>
+```
+
+`src/Hexalith.EventStore.AppHost` serves only this repository's own tests. A run of it is never evidence that
+EventStore runs in the Platform composition.
+

+## Run and Debug in the Platform Workspace
+
+EventStore runs and debugs as a module from the [Hexalith.Platform](https://github.com/Hexalith/Hexalith.Platform) workspace, where this repository is the `references/Hexalith.EventStore` submodule. From the Platform root, with the pinned module tool, Aspire CLI `13.6.1` exactly, Docker, and `HEXALITH_DAPR_HOME` pointing at an isolated Dapr home (CLI `1.18.0` at `tools/dapr`, runtime `1.18.2` in `.dapr/bin`):
+
+```bash
+dotnet tool restore
+dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- debug --manifest references/Hexalith.EventStore/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json
+dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- down --manifest references/Hexalith.EventStore/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json
+```
+
+`debug` builds `references/Hexalith.EventStore` in Debug, starts only the `eventstore` gateway with its Dapr sidecar, the Dapr control plane and Redis, waits for `/ready`, and reports the `dotnet run` launcher process id. Attach your debugger to the launcher's child process (`ps --ppid <launcher-pid> -o pid,args`). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#run-and-debug-in-the-platform-workspace) and the Platform README for the full prerequisites.
+
+`debug` does not print the run id: it is the file name of the run state `<runId>.json` under `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/hexalith-builds/g4-runs/` on Linux (newest: `ls -t "${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}"/hexalith-builds/g4-runs/*.json | head -1`). When an earlier run used the same manifest, `down --manifest` refuses with `HXR024`; add `--run-id <runId>`.

The docstring at `:44-51` states the helper probes "every checkout layout in the same order as the `$(Hexalith*Root)` auto-detection in `Directory.Build.props`" — that is false: `Directory.Build.props:23` puts `references/Hexalith.Tenants/src` first (with an explicit comment that it "takes precedence… over any sibling/standalone clone"), `:40` puts `references/Hexalith.Commons` first, and `grep -c 'MSBuildThisFileDirectory)Hexalith\.' Directory.Build.props` returns **0** — MSBuild has no root-level probe at all. Consequence: a stray root-level `Hexalith.Tenants/` directory silently shadows `references/Hexalith.Tenants`, which is exactly the root-level path assumption FR19 exists to retire, and the AppHost could launch a different csproj than it builds. Not patched because AC4 forbids replacing the flexible resolver absent a proven break, Dev Notes `:169` explicitly accepts it ("the required invariant is that `references/` remains the fallback/convention"), and AC1 verified no such directory exists today. Text-based stale-path scans structurally cannot see it because the path is composed via `Path.Combine`. Suggested durable fix, smallest first: correct the docstring to describe actual precedence; then reorder candidate 4 below `standalone` so `references/` wins, guarded by a test.
